discovery_target: Previously unreported autonomous sender-to-recipient coordination in which task work is transferred, used by a distinguishable recipient, and the cooperation crosses an operator-defined boundary
selection: Completed the exact thirty-record untouched nghttp2.org cursor saved by Pass 61. Every selected ID overlaps the pinned comparison release and had no listing-level decoded hash or feature cue. Original JSON revealed source-level structure in twenty-four records, so the assessment tested the strongest apparent message, navigation, response and account-group dependencies before rotating into seven exact committed-record locator queries.
snapshot_limitations: The sanitized snapshot preserves public report links, separate event and observation times, report and decoded-source hashes, domain-level traffic summaries, bounded static operation counts and one-way channel hashes. It omits submitted paths, visualization URLs, request and response bodies, headers, submitter values, credentials, personal addresses and recovered source. Scanner account or environment equality, source hashes and response hashes do not authenticate autonomous participants, task meaning, downstream use or an authorization boundary.

submit_provenance_equality.assessment: The two account identifiers are temporally separated but share an exact HTTP-test/Tableau source, one submission network-origin group and one exit-node group. This is compatible with account rotation or one research workflow on shared scanner infrastructure; it does not establish independent operators or autonomous participants.

strongest_apparent_dependencies.assessment: One source opens an AIHW visualization, registers a browser message listener and contains a best-effort fetch to example.com. The scanner archive records only the nghttp2 request: no message, outbound request, task result or recipient action is captured. Static capability inside one submitted page is not an exchange between autonomous participants.

One source queries Tableau worksheet-field metadata and serializes it into a navigation to example.com. The recorded request receives 404. This is a single submitted test program moving its own browser-observed metadata; there is no autonomous sender/recipient distinction, causal recipient use or operator-boundary evidence.

Four reports contain the same source across both scanner-account groups. It fetches a public HTTP-test response and calls a text parser, but discards the returned value; the surrounding action is an AIHW Tableau export-dialog test. Exact repetition supports a shared test template, not task-result transfer or adoption.

nghttp2_host_assessment.undecoded_records: Five records are redirects to the public AIHW visualization host, including Cloudflare challenge traffic in four. One record references Pie but preserves only nghttp2 error responses. None exposes decoded task material, a message body or recipient use.
nghttp2_host_assessment.legacy_feature_resolution: Seventeen records receive older listing features such as peer_language or repeated_requests. Source inspection resolves those cues to Tableau workbook/field-role APIs, UI labels, timers and ordinary HTTP-test repetition; the stricter task-or-peer lexical count is zero across the cohort.
nghttp2_host_assessment.assessment: The thirty records form a systematic browser-level test sequence around the already reported AIHW visualization family. They show filtering, export, popup/message and metadata-access experiments by submitted pages, not a sender-to-recipient task chain. All exact IDs already occur in the pinned comparison release, and no original record preserves distinct autonomous trajectories or unauthorized cooperation.
nghttp2_host_assessment.classification: Known AIHW comparison-overlap browser-test sequence; no autonomous transfer/use edge
